 Dangerous Speedometer Problem Prompts Recall of 102,000 of America’s Best-Selling Ford Trucks
 First for Autos Follow Jennifer Mashuga Fri, October 23, 2026 at 3:15 PM UTC Add to Preferred Sources Fri, October 23, 2026 at 3:15 PM UTC Ford Owners of Ford's best-selling F-Series pickups should take note: A newly announced recall covers a defect that could leave drivers unaware of how fast they're actually going.
 Ford Motor Company is recalling more than 102,000 trucks, Cars.com reported. The instrument panel's speedometer and tachometer can freeze, show inaccurate readings or otherwise malfunction. In a worst-case scenario, a driver who thinks they're traveling 50 mph could be going much faster.
 Ford hasn't reported any crashes or injuries tied to the issue. Still, a faulty speed reading raises the odds of a collision, not to mention a speeding ticket.
 Advertisement Advertisement The recall covers 2025-26 Super Duty F-250, F-350, F-450, F-550 and F-600 trucks, as well as model-year 2026 F-150s and Super Duty F-750s.
 Ford
 Since the problem isn't software-related, owners will need to take their trucks to a dealer. Ford dealerships will replace the instrument cluster module on every affected vehicle at no cost.
 Ford will mail notification letters to owners of affected vehicles on October 26. You don't have to wait, though. Enter your vehicle identification number (VIN) on Ford's recall website , or look up the recall on the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) website .
 Ford has had several recalls in recent months. In June 2026, the automaker recalled more than 400,000 vehicles over a seat belt defect and another 740,000 over transmission park problems that allowed vehicles to roll away. Between September and October, Ford also recalled vehicles for a headlight issue that reduced driver visibility.
